Periodic Tenancy Agreement (Assured Tenancy)
Tenant ID: NPM-404605   Prepared by Northgate Property Management

This is an assured periodic tenancy under the Housing Act 1988 as amended by the Renters' Rights Act 2025. It runs from month to month and there is no fixed term.

KEY TERMS

Landlord: Evergreen Locksmiths LLP of 237 Little Court, Bristol BS4 2AS

Tenant 1: Daryna Shevchenko
Tenant 2: Ben Poole

The Property:
Flat 4
78 St Mary's Gardens
Hackney
LONDON
EC1M 0XJ
together with the use in common with others of the entrance hall, stairs and communal areas.

Start date: 15/03/2025
Rent: £1,610.00 pcm
Deposit: £1,857.69 protected with the Deposit Protection Service
Agent: Northgate Property Management of 172 Ash View, Oxford, OX2 3WX

1A. Definitions and interpretation

(a) "Landlord" means Evergreen Locksmiths LLP and includes any person who later becomes entitled to the reversion of the Property.
(b) "Tenant" means Daryna Shevchenko and Ben Poole. Where there is more than one, the obligations are joint and several.
(c) "Property" means Flat 4, 78 St Mary's Gardens, Hackney, London EC1M 0XJ and includes the Fixtures and Fittings.
(d) "Rent" means £1,610.00 per month or such other sum as may be agreed or determined.
(e) "Deposit" means the sum of £1,857.69 held under clause 3.1.
(f) "Fixtures and Fittings" means the items listed in the Inventory.
(g) "Communal Areas" means the entrance, stairs, bin store and the communal Rose Garden.
(h) "Utilities" means gas, electricity, water, sewerage, telecommunications and broadband.
(i) "Agent" means Northgate Property Management or any other agent appointed by the Landlord.

TERMS AND CONDITIONS

## 2. Rent
2.1 If any Rent is unpaid for 14 days after it falls due, the Tenant will pay interest at 3% above the Bank of England base rate from the date it was due until the date it is paid, as permitted by the Renters' Rights Act 2025.

2.2 The Landlord may increase the Rent once a year by giving at least two months' written notice in the prescribed form under section 13 of the Housing Act 1988.

2.3 The Tenant is responsible for paying council tax, water and sewerage charges, gas, electricity, telephone, broadband and the television licence for the Property during the Term.

2.4 The Tenant agrees to pay the Rent monthly in advance without any deduction or set-off, whether or not formally demanded.

## 3. Deposit
3.1 A deposit of £1,857.69 is payable on signing. It will be registered with the Deposit Protection Service, an authorised tenancy deposit scheme, within 30 days.

3.2 Deductions from the Deposit must be itemised. Any dispute about deductions may be referred to the free dispute resolution service of the Deposit Protection Service.

3.3 No holding deposit is held. Where a holding deposit of £450.00 was paid it has been credited against the first month's Rent.

## 4. Tenant's obligations
4.1 To keep the interior of the Property, including the fixtures, fittings and items listed in the Inventory, in the same condition as at the start of the tenancy, fair wear and tear excepted.

4.2 The Tenant must not sublet the Property or allow anyone other than the persons named in this agreement to live there.

4.3 Pets: no pets are permitted other than one indoor cat which the Landlord has agreed to in writing.

4.4 Smoking is not permitted anywhere inside the Property, including the communal hallways.

4.5 The Tenant must be considerate to neighbours and must not play music or hold gatherings that can be heard outside the Property late at night.

4.6 To keep the garden tidy and the lawns cut, and not to remove any trees or shrubs. The communal areas, including the communal Rose Garden, are shared with other residents and must be kept clear.

4.7 Bins: the Tenant must use the bins provided and follow the council's collection schedule.

4.8 To heat and air the Property properly so that condensation does not build up, particularly in the bathroom and bedrooms.

4.9 Not to change the locks or have additional keys cut without consent, and to return all keys at the end of the tenancy.

4.10 No alterations: the Tenant must not paint, drill or alter the Property without permission.

4.11 The Tenant is advised to take out contents insurance. The Landlord is not liable for loss of the Tenant's belongings.

## 5. Landlord's obligations
5.1 The Landlord will not interfere with the Tenant's right to live in the Property peacefully.

5.2 Repairs: the Landlord is responsible for repairing the structure, exterior, drains, boiler, radiators, wiring and plumbing, in line with the Landlord and Tenant Act 1985.

5.3 The Landlord will arrange an annual gas safety check and provide the certificate within 28 days, as required by the Gas Safety (Installation and Use) Regulations 1998.

5.4 Smoke and carbon monoxide alarms have been tested on the first day of the tenancy and the Tenant will test them monthly.

5.5 To provide an electrical installation condition report dated no more than five years before the start of the tenancy.

5.6 The Tenant notes that the Mill Lane roadworks are scheduled during the Term; the Landlord will pass on any notices from the council.

## 6. Access
6.1 Access: on 24 hours' notice, except in an emergency, the Landlord may enter to inspect, repair or show the Property to prospective tenants in the last two months of the tenancy.

6.2 In an emergency the Landlord may enter the Property without notice.

6.3 The Agent will carry out a routine visit around every 6 months and send a short report to the Landlord. Inspections will normally take place every 6 months.

## 7. Ending the tenancy
7.1 On leaving, the Tenant will arrange a professional clean if the Property was professionally cleaned at the start, as recorded in the check-in report.

7.2 If neither party ends the tenancy at the end of the Term it will become a statutory periodic tenancy.

7.3 If the Tenant breaks the terms of this agreement, the Landlord may apply to the court for possession under the Housing Act 1988.

## 8. Furniture and appliances
8.1 Repairs to appliances provided by the Landlord will be arranged by the Agent within a reasonable time after they are reported.

8.2 Not to remove any furniture or effects belonging to the Landlord from the Property or store them outside.

## 9. Insurance
9.1 The buildings insurance is arranged by the Landlord. The Tenant must report any damage that could lead to an insurance claim as soon as possible.

9.2 If the Property is made uninhabitable by an insured risk, the Rent will stop being payable until it is fit to live in again, unless the damage was caused by the Tenant.

## 10. Notices
10.1 Notices to the Tenant may be served by leaving them at the Property or by email to the address given in Schedule 1. Any notice may be served by email, provided a copy is also sent by first class post.

10.2 For the purposes of sections 47 and 48 of the Landlord and Tenant Act 1987, notices may be served on the Landlord at: c/o Northgate Property Management, 172 Ash View, Oxford OX2 3WX.

## 11. Data protection
11.1 Personal data will be handled under the Data Protection Act 2018. The Agent's privacy notice is available on request.

## 12. General
12.1 Where there is more than one tenant, their obligations are joint and several. If two or more people are the Tenant, each is responsible for all the obligations, not just a share.

12.2 Nothing in this agreement is intended to give any third party rights under the Contracts (Rights of Third Parties) Act 1999. No one other than the parties may enforce this agreement.

12.3 The parties will try to resolve any disagreement informally before taking any further step.
